Opera today announced two new features for its desktop browser: optional vertical tabs and expanded Google Lens integration. Details below.

Opera One receives two updates

Opera today posted on its blog announcing two updates for the Opera One browser.

The first is an increasingly common browser interface setting: vertical tabs. It replaces the traditional horizontal tab bar with a side-by-side stacked layout, housed in a resizable panel.

Opera said, "When in use, you can see the favicon of the website, and more importantly, the full title — making it easy to identify each tab." In fact, users can choose to display full tab names or switch to an icon-only mode, freeing up more space for browsing content.

You can enable or disable the vertical tab bar from "Settings" under "Browser > Tabs".

In addition, Opera One has also expanded its earlier integration with Google Lens. Opera stated:

"Google Lens was previously built into Opera One, but we've made it more convenient and expanded its capabilities. You can now perform image searches directly from the Opera homepage, with Google Lens integrated into the search bar. You can also use local files or paste images from the clipboard to perform image searches. Clicking the Google Lens icon in the search bar brings up a dialog where you can provide an image by uploading a file, drag-and-drop, pasting from the clipboard, or entering an image URL. Search results will be displayed in your current tab."
